title: Maharashtra, West Bengal, Punjab, Bihar and Puducherry — filling the gaps
selection: VacayOut's guides for Maharashtra, West Bengal, Punjab, Bihar and Puducherry covered only a few places (no Kolkata, Ajanta, Ellora or Pune; no Pondicherry town page). This pack adds the main cities and sights of each, with itineraries, researched from Incredible India (Ministry of Tourism) and UNESCO.

MH1.claim: Maharashtra has 5 UNESCO World Heritage Sites, including the Ajanta, Ellora and Elephanta caves.

evidence.quote: The state takes pride in its wealth of historical wonders that reflect the grandeur of bygone eras with 5 UNESCO World Heritage Sites.

MH_FOOD.claim: Eat vada pav on Mumbai's streets and a traditional Maharashtrian thali.

evidence.quote: Savor the spicy Vada Pav on the bustling streets of Mumbai, relish the traditional Maharashtrian thali

evidence.quote: Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj International Airport (BOM)

SN1.claim: Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar, formerly Aurangabad, is the base for Ellora and for Ajanta, about 100 km away.

evidence.quote: Once known as Aurangabad, this city has reclaimed its Maratha heritage
about 100 kilometres from the city lies the marvellous Ajanta Caves

SN2.claim: The best time to visit is November to March, when the weather is mild.

evidence.quote: The ideal time to embark on a journey to Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar is between November and March, when the weather is delightfully mild

SN3.claim: The city once had 52 historic gates; shop for Paithani sarees at Gul Mandi and Paithan Gate.

evidence.quote: the 52 historic gates that once guarded this majestic city
Immerse yourself in the kaleidoscope of colours and textures at Gul Mandi and Paithan Gate, where exquisite Paithani sarees

ELL1.claim: Ellora's 34 caves are Buddhist, Hindu and Jain temples and monasteries cut into the rock between the 6th and 10th centuries.

evidence.quote: a testament to the brilliance of Buddhist, Hindu, and Jain monks and artisans who dedicated themselves to this endeavour between the 6th and 10th centuries
Explore the 34 captivating caves

ELL2.claim: The Kailasa Temple, dedicated to Shiva, took over a century to carve and is the largest rock-cut temple of its kind.

evidence.quote: This colossal rock-cut temple, taking over a century to complete, is the largest of its kind globally.

ELL3.claim: An evening light and sound show runs in English and Hindi.

evidence.quote: attend the mesmerising light and sound show held in the evenings
presented in both English and Hindi

AJ1.claim: Ajanta's first Buddhist caves date from the 2nd and 1st centuries BC; more richly decorated caves were added in the Gupta period.

evidence.quote: The first Buddhist cave monuments at Ajanta date from the 2nd and 1st centuries B.C.
During the Gupta period (5th and 6th centuries A.D.), many more richly decorated caves were added to the original group.

AJ2.claim: Ajanta's paintings and sculptures are counted among the masterpieces of Buddhist religious art.

evidence.quote: The paintings and sculptures of Ajanta, considered masterpieces of Buddhist religious art, have had a considerable artistic influence.

DAU1.claim: Daulatabad (Deogiri) Fort, 15 km from Ellora, dates to the 12th century; about 750 steps lead to the top.

evidence.quote: Located just 15 kilometres from Ellora Caves, Daulatabad Fort is a mediaeval fortress that dates back to the 12th century.
To reach the summit, adventurers must ascend approximately 750 steps

DAU2.claim: The fort's Chand Minar tower is over 63 m tall, and a 30 m deep moat once guarded it.

evidence.quote: the awe-inspiring Chand Minar, a tower that reaches a staggering height of over 63 meters
One of its most striking features is the 30-meter-deep moat

GRI1.claim: Grishneshwar, near Ellora, is revered as the 12th Jyotirlinga; men remove their shirts to enter the sanctum.

evidence.quote: revered as the 12th and final Jyotirlinga of India
Men are requested to remove their shirts before entering

GRI2.claim: Aarti is held at 5:30 am, 12 noon, 7 pm and 9:30 pm.

evidence.quote: Aarti timings are 5:30 AM, 12:00 PM, 7:00 PM, and 9:30 PM

PUN1.claim: Pune mixes Maratha history and a modern city; Sinhagad Fort above it offers wide views.

evidence.quote: Pune is a city where history and modernity coalesce seamlessly
This ancient fortress, perched atop a hill, offers panoramic views of the surrounding landscape

PUN2.claim: The best time to visit Pune is October to February.

evidence.quote: The best time to visit Pune is between October and February when the weather is pleasantly cool

SHW1.claim: Shaniwar Wada is an 18th-century palace-fort in the heart of Pune; the rock-cut Pataleshwar Cave Temple is about 2 km away.

evidence.quote: Shaniwar Wada in Pune, India, is an enchanting historical masterpiece constructed during the 18th century
Situated approximately two kilometres from Shaniwar Wada

AGA1.claim: Built by Aga Khan III in 1892, the palace held Mahatma Gandhi, Kasturba Gandhi and others prisoner during the Quit India Movement; it is now a museum.

evidence.quote: Constructed by Sultan Muhammed Shah Aga Khan III
in 1892, its history draws tourists from around the globe
Mahatma Gandhi, Kasturba Gandhi, Mahadev Desai and Sarojini Naidu were all imprisoned within its walls for two years
Today, the Aga Khan Palace has been transformed into an unforgettable museum

MAB1.claim: Mahabaleshwar is a hill station at about 4,500 ft in the Sahyadris, with a 500-year-old Shiva temple; Panchgani is 20 km away.

evidence.quote: Perched beautifully at an altitude of 4500 feet
the 500-year-old Mahabaleshwar Temple here, a revered sanctuary dedicated to Lord Shiva
its twin town just 20 kilometres away

MAB2.claim: In strawberry season, stalls sell strawberry shakes, jams and more.

evidence.quote: Strawberry season finds its streets full of vendors selling an array of strawberry products, including strawberry shakes, jams and more.

PRA1.claim: Pratapgad Fort near Mahabaleshwar was built under Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj; his battle with Afzal Khan took place at its base.

evidence.quote: Welcome to Pratapgad Fort, the majestic citadel near Mahabaleshwar
The most renowned tale recounts the epic battle between Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj and Afzal Khan at the fort's base.

NSK1.claim: Nashik, on the Godavari, hosts the Kumbh Mela every 12 years and is linked to Rama's exile.

evidence.quote: renowned for hosting the Kumbh Mela, the largest spiritual gathering on earth, every 12 years
Nashik is situated on the banks of the holy Godavari River

NSK2.claim: Nashik is known as India's wine capital; Trimbakeshwar Shiva temple is in the hills nearby.

evidence.quote: it is known as the wine capital of India
a celestial abode of Lord Shiva nestled amidst the tranquil hills of Nashik

PAN1.claim: Panchavati is the Ramayana-era site of Nashik, with the Ramkund bathing ghat on the Godavari; visit December to March.

evidence.quote: known as Panchvati during the period of Ramayana
Begin your spiritual quest in the hallowed waters of Ramkund
December to March is the best time to visit Panchvati.

KLP1.claim: Kolhapur is famous for Kolhapuri chappals; its 19th-century New Palace mixes European and Indian styles.

evidence.quote: the world-famous Kolhapuri chappals (sandals)
erected in the 19th century by Chhatrapati Shahu Maharaj, displays a stunning amalgamation of European and Indian styles

MLX1.claim: The 7th-century Mahalakshmi (Ambabai) Temple is one of the Shakti Peethas, built in the Hemadpanti style.

evidence.quote: This masterpiece of Deccan design, dating back to the 7th century AD
it holds pride of place among 108 Shakti Peethas
Embellished with Hemadpanti architecture

WB1.claim: Durga Puja is West Bengal's most loved festival, with elaborate pandals across the state.

evidence.quote: Durga Puja reigning as the region's most beloved celebration
adorning elaborate tents known as "pandals" across the state

WB2.claim: West Bengal's heritage runs from Bishnupur's terracotta temples to the ancient capital of Gour and Kolkata's Victoria Memorial.

evidence.quote: From the majestic terracotta temples of Bishnupur, adorned with intricate sculptures, to the iconic Victoria Memorial in Kolkata
Explore the architectural wonders of the ancient capital, Gour

WB3.claim: The Sundarbans is a UNESCO World Heritage Site; the hills have Darjeeling's tea gardens.

evidence.quote: The Sunderbans, a UNESCO World Heritage Site, showcases the unique coexistence of man and nature.
the lush tea gardens of Darjeeling and the dense mangrove forests of the Sundarbans promise breathtaking landscapes

KOL1.claim: Kolkata's landmarks include the Howrah Bridge, New Market, the Victoria Memorial and the Maidan; Tagore's Rabindra Sangeet is part of its culture.

evidence.quote: From the iconic Howrah Bridge to the vibrant bustle of New Market, Kolkata is home to numerous famous spots
the sprawling grounds of the Maidan, where locals gather to relax and unwind
Especially the soulful music of Nobel laureate Rabindranath Tagore, known as Rabindra Sangeet.

KOL2.claim: Durga Puja is one of India's grandest celebrations.

evidence.quote: And no visit is complete without experiencing the festive spirit of Durga Puja, one of the grandest celebrations in the country.

VIC1.claim: The white-marble Victoria Memorial was built 1906–1921 in 64 acres of gardens and has 25 galleries.

evidence.quote: This architectural masterpiece, built between 1906 and 1921, spans an impressive 64 acres of meticulously curated gardens.
explore its 25 distinct galleries

HOW1.claim: Howrah Bridge over the Hooghly opened on 3 February 1943 and is the world's busiest cantilever bridge.

evidence.quote: Finally, on February 3rd, 1943, the Howrah Bridge, a testament to human ingenuity, was inaugurated
it is the busiest cantilever bridge in the world

DAK1.claim: Dakshineswar Kali Temple on the Hooghly was built by Rani Rashmoni; its idols were installed on 31 May 1855.

evidence.quote: It is said that the famed Bengal Queen, Rani Rashmoni sanctioned the building of this temple.
On 31st May 1855

BEL1.claim: Belur Math, headquarters of the Ramakrishna movement, was consecrated by Swami Vivekananda in 1898; he spent his last years here.

evidence.quote: consecrated the grounds in 1898 with the sacred relics of his revered guru
it was here that Swami Vivekananda, one of the foremost thinkers and religious leaders of the present age, spent the final years of his remarkable life

IM1.claim: The Indian Museum, established in 1814, holds Buddhist sculpture, miniature paintings and even a dinosaur egg.

evidence.quote: an iconic institution established in 1814
view an authentic dinosaur egg
exquisite ancient Buddhist sculptures, delicate Indian miniature paintings

KGT1.claim: Kalighat is the temple of the goddess Kali; the present building dates from the 19th century.

evidence.quote: The temple was built as an abode for the Hindu Goddess Kali.
However, what stands today is said to be as young as the 19th century.

CS1.claim: College Street, or Boi Para, is Kolkata's famous book market, named after Hindu College, founded in 1817.

evidence.quote: also known as Boi Para (which translates to
traces back to the establishment of Hindu College in 1817 by David Hare

KLM1.claim: Kalimpong is a hill station at 1,250 m with the Zang Dhok Palri Phodang monastery and a cactus nursery of over 3,000 varieties.

evidence.quote: Perched at an altitude of 1,250 meters, this beautiful hill station is a great getaway to unwind and relax.
No visit to Kalimpong would be complete without a visit to the renowned Zang Dhok Palri Phodang monastery.
an impressive collection of over 3,000 varieties of cacti and succulents

DEOL1.claim: Deolo Hill above Kalimpong has views of the Kanchenjunga range and a flower park at the top.

evidence.quote: where you'll be rewarded with panoramic vistas of the majestic Kanchenjunga range
At the summit of the hill, there is a park built for recreational purposes, featuring exotic flowers.

SUN1.claim: The Sundarbans covers 10,000 sq km of the Ganges delta (more than half in India) and has the world's largest mangrove forest, home to tigers.

evidence.quote: The Sundarbans covers 10,000 km 2 of land and water (more than half of it in India, the rest in Bangladesh) in the Ganges delta.
It contains the world's largest area of mangrove forests.
A number of rare or endangered species live in the park, including tigers, aquatic mammals, birds and reptiles.

SAN1.claim: Rabindranath Tagore founded Santiniketan in 1901; the Visva Bharati 'world university' followed in 1921.

evidence.quote: Established in rural West Bengal in 1901 by the renowned poet and philosopher Rabindranath Tagore
was established at Santiniketan in 1921

PB1.claim: Punjabi food to try: butter chicken, dal makhani, and makki di roti with sarson da saag.

evidence.quote: Savour the authentic flavours of Punjab, with dishes like butter chicken, dal makhani, and makki di roti with sarson da saag.

PB2.claim: Harike Wetland, where the Beas and Sutlej meet, is northern India's largest wetland and home to the endangered Indus river dolphin.

evidence.quote: Located at the confluence of the Beas and Sutlej rivers, Harike Wetland and Bird Sanctuary is home to a variety of bird species, including the endangered Indus river dolphin.
Birdwatchers will be delighted by the avian diversity at the largest wetland in northern India.

PB3.claim: Amritsar is known for its markets, street food and the Wagah Border ceremony.

evidence.quote: Amritsar is a bustling city known for its vibrant markets, delectable street food, and the Wagah Border Ceremony

PAT1.claim: Patiala, founded by Baba Ala Singh of the Phulkian state, grew around Qila Mubarak, begun in 1763.

evidence.quote: Founded by Baba Ala Singh, the visionary who established the Phulkian State
In 1763, he laid the foundation of the Patiala Fort, known as Qila Mubarak, around which the city developed.

PAT2.claim: Patiala is known for embroidered parandas (hair cords); Baradari Gardens has rare trees and colonial buildings.

evidence.quote: waist cords and Parandas (hair-tying cords)
Baradari Gardens , a stunning garden complex that boasts rare trees, colonial buildings

QM1.claim: Qila Mubarak, Patiala's fort, was begun in 1763 and shows Sikh palace architecture.

evidence.quote: In 1763, he laid the foundation of the Patiala Fort, known as Qila Mubarak
provide you with a rare glimpse into Sikh palace architecture

SHM1.claim: Patiala's Sheesh Mahal, the 'Palace of Mirrors', was built 1845–1862 by Maharaja Narinder Singh.

evidence.quote: located in the heart of Patiala, Punjab
Constructed between 1845 and 1862 by Maharaja Narinder Singh

KPT1.claim: Kapurthala is known for the Indo-Saracenic Jagatjit Palace and its Moorish Mosque.

evidence.quote: Kapurthala boasts an eclectic collection of monuments and gardens
a captivating example of Indo-Saracenic architecture
the Moorish Mosque offers a glimpse into a unique blend of architectural styles

FGS1.claim: Fatehgarh Sahib is named after Sahibzada Fateh Singh, younger son of Guru Gobind Singh; its gurdwara remembers him, Zorawar Singh and Mata Gujri.

evidence.quote: the town derives its name from Sahibzada Fateh Singh, the younger son of Guru Gobind Singh Ji
built in memory of Sahibzada Fateh Singh, Sahibzada Zorawar Singh, and Mata Gujri Ji

BR1.claim: Bihar is the birthplace of Buddhism and Jainism.

evidence.quote: This ancient land is the birthplace of two of the world's major religions, Buddhism and Jainism

BR2.claim: Chhath, Bihar's best-known festival, falls between late October and mid-November and lasts up to four days.

evidence.quote: typically falling between late October and mid-November, spanning a celebration of up to four days

BR3.claim: Madhubani painting is Bihar's best-known art.

evidence.quote: Among Bihar's artistic traditions, the works of Madhubani artists stand out.

PTN1.claim: Patna, ancient Pataliputra, has roots going back to 600 BC and lies along the Ganges.

evidence.quote: The capital of Bihar is a modern city with ancient roots going back to 600 BC.
then known as Pataliputra, was renowned as one of the great cities of Asia

PTN2.claim: The Patna Museum displays a 15 m fossilised tree trunk believed to be 200 million years old.

evidence.quote: The museum also boasts a 15-m (49-ft) long fossilized tree trunk, believed to be 200 million years old.

TPS1.claim: Takht Sri Patna Sahib, one of Sikhism's five takhts, marks the birthplace of Guru Gobind Singh; a museum above the sanctum holds relics.

evidence.quote: comprises five Gurudwaras known for their religious significance within Sikhism
At the heart of this hallowed sanctuary lies the birthplace of the revered Sri Guru Gobind Singh Ji Maharaj
On the floor above the main sanctum is a museum with the guru

BMU1.claim: The Bihar Museum covers 5.6 hectares; its galleries opened between 2015 and 2017 and trace the Maurya and Gupta empires, Buddhism and Jainism.

evidence.quote: Over its total 5.6 hectares of land and 24,000-square-metre built-up area
culminating with unveiling of remaining galleries in October 2017
Visitors can gain an understanding of Buddhism and Jainism spread as well as that of Gupta Dynasty, Mauryan Dynasty

GOL1.claim: Gol Ghar, a 29 m granary dome, was built in 1786 under Warren Hastings after the famine of 1770.

evidence.quote: Built in 1786 on the orders of the first Governor-General of India, Warren Hastings
as a response to the famine of 1770
rising at an impressive height of 29 metres

KES1.claim: Kesaria Stupa was commissioned by Emperor Ashoka to mark the Buddha's visit; Xuanzang described it in the 7th century.

evidence.quote: Commissioned by Emperor Ashoka to commemorate Buddha's visit
7th century diary records his visit to Kesaria Stupa site

PY1.claim: Pondicherry, on the south-east coast about 170 km from Chennai, was the capital of French India; Karaikal, Mahe and Yanam joined it as a Union Territory.

evidence.quote: The city sits on the southeastern coast of India, about 170 kms from Chennai.
Puducherry, formerly known as Pondicherry, gained its significance as
Pondicherry, along with Karaikal, Mahe and Yanam, was constituted as a Union Territory in the Indian Union.

PY2.claim: Sri Aurobindo Ashram was founded in 1926 by Sri Aurobindo and the Mother.

evidence.quote: Sri Aurobindo Ashram, a spiritual community founded in 1926 by Sri Aurobindo and the Mother

PY3.claim: Promenade Beach has a long seafront walk; Paradise Beach is the other well-known beach.

evidence.quote: Promenade Beach, with its long waterfront promenade, and Paradise Beach are some of the more noticeable ones.

PY4.claim: Food ranges from croissants and pizza to dosa and seafood.

evidence.quote: From freshly baked Pizzas and croissants to typical South Indian Dosa and a variety of seafood, Puducherry is a food lover's delight.

PYM1.claim: The museum has one of the largest collections of Chola bronzes, Roman-era trade finds and French furniture.

evidence.quote: one of the largest collection of Chola bronze sculptures
These illustrate the significance of Pondicherry as a port of trade between the first and second centuries AD.

PAR1.claim: Paradise Beach is reached by a short boat ride from Chunnambar Boat House, which offers paddle and motor boats.

evidence.quote: the pristine Paradise Beach that can be reached via a short and scenic boat ride
Boating is the most popular choice, with options ranging from paddle boats to motor boats

NDA1.claim: Notre Dame des Anges on the Promenade was built in 1855 and holds services in French, Tamil and English.

evidence.quote: Located along the famous Promenade of Pondicherry, this church was crafted by the skilled hands of Louis Guerre in 1855.
it is the world's only church where prayers resonate in French, Tamil, and English

FWM1.claim: The French War Memorial on the seafront was inaugurated on 3 April 1938 and rebuilt in 1970; it honours French Indian soldiers of the World Wars.

evidence.quote: Governor Crocicchia inaugurated this memorial on April 3, 1938
Reconstructed in 1970
A bronze plaque lists the names of those who gave their lives during World War I
